title: Racemose vs Cymose Explained Simply | PUC Biology Class 11
description:
A stalk of yellow mustard flowers, a bunch of jasmine and a big sunflower are each many flowers in a pattern. Diya notices that on mustard the open flowers are at the bottom, but on jasmine the middle flower opened first.

You will see why a flower is a modified shoot, then watch a racemose axis keep growing and add flowers in acropetal order, and a cymose axis end in a flower and add younger flowers below in basipetal order, with mustard and jasmine as examples. Then the two types side by side, a pause and think check, a worked sorting example, the exam trap on acropetal, an original NEET statement question and a recap card.

This is Episode 43 of our PUC Biology series.

Made for NCERT, CBSE, ISC (CISCE), PUC (Karnataka) and NEET students.

In this video:
0:00 Mustard, jasmine and a sunflower
0:32 A flower is a modified shoot
1:03 Racemose: the axis keeps growing
1:31 Cymose: the axis ends in a flower
2:02 Racemose vs cymose + pause and think
2:47 Worked example: sort the clues
3:11 Exam trap: what acropetal means
3:35 Practice question (NEET pattern)
4:02 Recap and three questions
